- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The French language has been influenced by Latin, Germanic languages, Arabic, English, Italian, Celtic languages, Spanish, Dutch, Portuguese, Greek, Breton, and Yiddish.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Latin was the official language of the Roman Empire and significantly influenced French, especially in science, law, and religion.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Germanic tribes, including the Franks and Normans, influenced Old French, which is still reflected in modern French.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Arabic contributed words like “cotton,” “sugar,” and “coffee” to the French language.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] English has significantly influenced French, particularly in technology and popular culture.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Italian Renaissance impacted French culture and language, leading to the adoption of words like “ciao” and “fresco.”
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Celtic languages contributed loanwords to French prior to the Roman conquest.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Spanish has influenced French, especially in regions bordering Spain, with borrowed words and expressions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Dutch words have been adopted into French, particularly in commerce and sailing.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Portuguese has influenced French through trade, with words related to sailing like "bateau" (boat) and "cabestan" (capstan).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Greek has impacted French, especially in science and medicine, with many technical terms derived from it.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Breton language has influenced French, particularly in agriculture and food.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Yiddish has contributed several words to French, particularly related to food and culture.
